READ_THIS_BEFORE_READING_ANY_OTHER_KEY.theMistakeThisBlockExistsToPrevent: Freeze section 7.3 and CMP-IR-01: a derivation must be RESOLVED, not read. Checking whether a candidate carried a block by looking for it as a top-level key of the delta file returns ABSENT when the block is operation N of M. The freeze records that reading a derivation instead of resolving it produced a wrong answer FIVE times in this corpus.
READ_THIS_BEFORE_READING_ANY_OTHER_KEY.soIfYouAreLookingForAKey: Use $.keyLocator. It lists every top-level key of the RESOLVED document and says, for each, whether this derivation changes it and at which operation, or whether it is inherited unchanged and therefore absent from this file. A grep against these bytes answers a different question than the one you are asking.
READ_THIS_BEFORE_READING_ANY_OTHER_KEY.andIfYouWantToKnowYouResolvedItCorrectly: $.resolvedValue.sha256 is the SHA-256 of the canonical serialisation of the resolved value. Reproduce it. If it does not match, your resolution is not this one.

whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.theDecidingReason: The predecessor is 64 kB and most of it is RECORDED MEASUREMENT: 13 executable counterexample fixtures with observed checker output, 27 recorded inputs with digests, a three-item assessment each citing an artifact, its recomputed digest and the review that judged those exact bytes. A standalone successor would have to retype all of it. Freeze section 7.2.2 is a record of what happens when a lane republishes a measurement it did not take: six stale entries in one knownLimitations block, one of them instructing the next reviewer to verify a withdrawn number. A derivation cannot commit that error, because it transcribes nothing.
whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.theStructuralGuarantee: A derivation can only change what its operations name. Every position not named by an operation is inherited by resolution and is therefore byte-identical by construction, not by promise. That is a guarantee a standalone re-author cannot make about a 64 kB document.
whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.theCostAndWhyItIsPaid: The cost is that this file cannot be read as the document, and this corpus has paid that cost wrongly five times. It is paid here with three mitigations the failing cases lacked: a first-key warning, a keyLocator that answers the exact question the failed greps were asking, and a reproducible digest of the resolved value so a reader can prove they resolved it the same way.
whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.whatWouldHaveMadeStandaloneRight: If the decision had invalidated the fixtures, the assessment and the recorded inputs together, there would be little left to inherit and a standalone would be honest. It does not. It falsifies eleven prose positions and three recorded measurements out of a document whose bulk is untouched.

derivation.predecessorParsedWith: json.loads(..., object_pairs_hook=<duplicate-key rejecting>) per freeze section 7.5. Zero duplicate keys at any depth.
derivation.whyThisBaseAndNotAnother: v10-disposition.v1 is the only version of this base on disk. It carries no independent review, so no verdict binds its bytes; it is nevertheless not edited, because freeze section 7.2's repair form is a successor and the predecessor's recorded measurements have to stay readable as measurements of their own moment.

resolutionAlgorithm.step1: Parse v10-disposition.v1.json with a duplicate-key-rejecting object_pairs_hook. Refuse on any duplicate.
resolutionAlgorithm.step2: Verify sha256(predecessor bytes) equals predecessorSha256. Refuse on mismatch.
resolutionAlgorithm.step3: Apply $.derivation.operations in array order to a deep copy.
resolutionAlgorithm.step4: For op 'set': navigate path, require the target to EXIST, and require its current value to be strictly equal to 'from'. Refuse otherwise.
resolutionAlgorithm.step5: For op 'add': navigate path, require the parent object to exist and the final key to be ABSENT. Refuse otherwise.
resolutionAlgorithm.step6: Refusal is total. A resolver that cannot satisfy every operation produces NO document; it never produces a partial one.
resolutionAlgorithm.pathGrammar: 'path' is an ARRAY of tokens: a JSON string is an object key, a JSON integer is a zero-based array index. There is no grammar to get wrong. 'pathDisplay' is a rendering for human readers and is NOT normative.
resolutionAlgorithm.strictEqualityRule: Strict equality is TYPE-EXACT and tests bool BEFORE int. In Python bool subclasses int, so True == 1 and isinstance(True, int) are both true; a 'from' guard written with == alone would accept an integer respelling of a boolean. versioning-policy.v9's independent review measured exactly that hole - 15 of 139 boolean leaves admitted an integer respelling at exit 0 - and this rule is written to be immune to it.
resolutionAlgorithm.keyOrder: Operations of kind 'add' append at the end of their parent object, so the resolved document's key order differs from the predecessor's. The canonical serialisation sorts keys, so the published digest is unaffected by order. No claim is made about any file's byte order.
